results.title: S. Korea, US top diplomats discuss N. Korea, bilateral issues in Paris
results.content: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun met with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in France on Tuesday to discuss North Korea and bilateral issues, Seoul's foreign ministry said. Cho held a pull-aside meeting with Rubio on the sidelines of a Group of Seven (G7) foreign ministers' meeting and "exchanged views on overall bilateral relations, high-level exchanges and North Korea-related issues," the ministry said, without disclosing other details. Tuesday's meeting marked the first in-person encounter between the two foreign ministers since the results of the U.S. midterm elections were announced on Nov. 4. The meeting came as the South Korean Cabinet approved a bill earlier in the day seeking parliamentary consent for the government's plan to expand the operational scope of its anti-piracy Cheonghae unit from waters off the Somali coast to areas closer to the Strait of Hormuz. results.title: Financial Security Institute reports data leak following hacking attack
results.content: Korea's state-run Financial Security Institute (FSI) reported a data leak following a hacking attack targeting its security assessment system, officials said Tuesday. The FSI, which oversees financial information provided by banks and insurers, detected the breach the previous day, according to financial authorities. The leaked information reportedly came from the FSI's website used to conduct security assessments of financial institutions. Officials said some information related to the security status submitted by financial firms may have been compromised in the breach.

results.title: Defense chief reiterates need to integrate military academies
results.content: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul on Tuesday reiterated the need to integrate the Army, Navy and Air Force academies into a single institution, saying the reform is essential to preparing the military for future warfare, his office said. Kang made the remarks during a meeting with about 60 cadets from the three academies at the Korea Military Academy in northern Seoul to gather their views on the government's integration plan. During the meeting, Kang reiterated his support for establishing the tentatively named National Military Academy to better prepare future officers for evolving warfare and strengthen the country's long-term security. He added that the location of the proposed academy remained under consideration. An Army cadet argued that military education reform should be distinguished from past misconduct by some Army officers, citing President Lee Jae Myung's remarks in August li

results.title: BOK chief Shin Hyun-song tapped to lead BIS committee on payment systems
results.content: Bank of Korea (BOK) Gov. Shin Hyun-song has been tapped to lead a major committee on payment and related financial market infrastructure at the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), his office said Tuesday. Shin was named chairman of the Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures (CPMI) following consultations among members at the BIS Global Economy Meeting (GEM), according to the BOK. His three-year term began on Nov. 1. The CPMI is an international standards-setting body dedicated to enhancing the stability and efficiency of payment systems and financial market infrastructure. It also serves as a key consultative body among central banks under the BIS GEM. Shin is the first non-American and non-European to chair the CPMI since the committee was established in 1990 as the Committee on Payment and Settlement Systems. With Shin's appointment, the BOK is expected to strengthen it

results.title: Korean parents enlist ghosts to discipline kids, sparking child abuse complaints
results.content: A popular attraction at the Korean Folk Village, where actors dressed as ghosts discipline misbehaving children, has come under scrutiny after complaints prompted the local government to consider investigating possible child abuse. The move has instead sparked controversy, with many online commenters arguing that parents who bring their children to the attraction, rather than the folk village itself, should be held responsible if the experience is deemed abusive. Yongin City, Gyeonggi Province, said Monday that it plans to visit the Korean Folk Village later this month with child welfare experts and police to examine how the so-called "ghost discipline" event is operated. Every autumn, the folk village hosts an event featuring actors dressed as traditional Korean ghosts, including the nine-tailed fox and the virgin ghost. results.title: First lady Kim meets with Korean women in Japan
results.content: First lady Kim Hea Kyung met Tuesday with female members of an association representing Korean residents in Japan and praised the group's contributions to the development of their home country. Kim, wife of President Lee Jae Myung, made the remarks during an afternoon tea meeting with members of the women's division of the Korean Residents Union in Japan, also known as "Mindan" in Korean. The first lady thanked the compatriots for their service to their home country, saying, "You have worried about and lent support when Korea was in trouble and cheered more enthusiastically than anyone when it grew and developed." The first lady said the compatriots' enduring love had helped make Korea what it is today. "We will cherish our gratitude for a long time," she said, welcoming their visit to their home country. results.title: Actor Zo In-sung embraces artistic challenge in 'Possible Love'
results.content: For actor Zo In-sung, starring in master director Lee Chang-dong’s latest movie "Possible Love" means both a career peak and a profound journey of self-discovery. "Possible Love,” which clinched the Silver Lion Grand Jury Prize at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival and has been selected as Korea’s official entry for International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards, centers on two couples whose lives collide during a documentary project, exposing hidden desires and social divides. In the Netflix original film, the 45-year-old actor plays Sang-woo, a wealthy heir who embodies a multilayered nature of capital and power. "Working with director Lee came as a complete surprise," Zo told The Korea Times during an interview at a cafe in Seoul on Tuesday. results.title: DPK, liberal lawmakers propose bill allowing overseas Koreans to vote electronically
results.content: A bill allowing Koreans living overseas to vote electronically has been proposed by ruling and minor party lawmakers, parliamentary records showed Tuesday, in a move aimed at improving voting accessibility. The proposed revision to the Public Official Election Act would allow voters to cast their ballots in presidential and parliamentary elections without having to visit designated polling stations, according to the National Assembly's online bill information system. The bill, led by Rep. Kim Young-ho of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), was proposed Friday, co-sponsored by 11 other DPK lawmakers and Rep. Kim Joon-hyung of the minor Rebuilding Korea Party. By introducing an electronic voting system operated by the National Election Commission (NEC), the bill seeks to address challenges faced by Koreans living far from overseas polling stations. results.title: Korean won gains against US dollar as oil prices slide
results.content: The Korean won climbed against the U.S. dollar Tuesday, as global oil prices declined with U.S. President Donald Trump signaling a possible resolution to the war with Iran. The won was quoted at 1,337.5 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., up 9.6 won from the close of the previous stock trading session. After meeting with Qatar Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, a key mediator between Washington and Tehran, at the White House, Trump told reporters that further strikes against Iran will not be necessary for the time being. The won's advance also got a boost from a sharp rebound in the stock market, with foreign investors turning to net buyers of local stocks. results.title: Seoul Metro union threatens Nov. 25 general strike over wage, hiring disputes
results.content: The largest of three labor unions at Seoul Metro threatened Tuesday to launch a general strike on Nov. 25 unless its demands, including additional staff recruitment and wage increases, are met. Union 1 of Seoul Metro, which operates subway Lines 1-8 and parts of Line 9, issued the warning at a news conference following a meeting of senior union members. The union initially sought a 5.2 percent wage increase but lowered its demand to 3.5 percent in negotiations with management. It also calls for scrapping a plan to cut 2,212 jobs and hiring an additional 1,313 workers this year to address staff shortages. Other demands include state funding for public services and a requirement that all field work be performed by two-person teams. The union said 7,782, or 84.6 percent, of its 9,201 members recently participated in a vote, with 6,715, or 86.3 percent of those who voted, backing the strike

results.title: Korean stocks surge over 4% as risk appetite returns
results.content: Korean stocks surged more than 4 percent, Tuesday, as easing Middle East tensions and an overnight rally in U.S. semiconductor shares revived risk appetite. The benchmark closed at 5,239.13, up 4.39 percent. It opened 4.55 percent higher, triggering a buy-side sidecar at 9:06 a.m, but pared some of the early gains. Foreign investors turned net buyers for the first time in eight trading sessions, purchasing a net 353.2 billion won ($264.3 million) of shares. Institutional investors also bought a net 498 billion won, while retail investors sold a net 1.34 trillion won. Semiconductor stocks helped lift the index. SK hynix surged 6.69 percent to close at 1,212,000 won, while Samsung Electronics climbed 4.74 percent to 198,900 won. results.title: [COVER STORY] Iran sees Cheonghae expansion as backing US war effort
results.content: Korea is facing a diplomatic challenge in convincing Iran that the Cheonghae Unit’s expanded mission closer to the Strait of Hormuz is not an intervention in the ongoing U.S.-Iran war, as the Middle Eastern country warned Korea could be “portrayed as an accomplice” of U.S. military attacks. Although Korea’s defense authorities reiterated that the unit's expanded duties do not cover the strait but rather are aimed at protecting Korean vessels from piracy, experts say it seems Seoul’s message has not been delivered as intended. This raises concerns that Iran could view the move as entry into the war and lead to potential clashes. results.title: Korea's export boom masks widening gap between large, small firms
results.content: Korea’s exports surged more than 70 percent in the third quarter from a year earlier, but much of the growth was concentrated among a handful of large corporations, widening the gap between major exporters and smaller businesses, government data showed Tuesday. While shipments soared, the number of exporting firms remained virtually unchanged, suggesting that the benefits of the export boom have yet to spread across the business sector. According to preliminary trade statistics released by the Ministry of Data and Statistics and the Korea Customs Service, exports jumped 72.3 percent year-on-year to $318.6 billion in the third quarter. Imports rose 25 percent to $203.1 billion. results.title: N. Korea rejects UN chief's call for inter-Korean dialogue after mine blast
results.content: North Korea on Tuesday rejected U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres' recent call to resume inter-Korean dialogue to ease tensions following September's mine blast near the border, accusing him of being "prejudiced and irresponsible." Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, made the rejection in a statement carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). Last week, the U.N. chief called for restoring communication channels between South and North Korea amid concerns over a potential escalation of tensions following the Sept. 21 explosion inside the Demilitarized Zone. That incident, blamed on mines planted by the North, wounded three South Korean soldiers, two of them seriously. results.title: OPCON transfer unlikely during Trump's term, ex-US diplomat says
results.content: The transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) from the United States to South Korea is unlikely to happen during the remaining two years of the Trump administration, former acting U.S. Ambassador to South Korea Joseph Yun said Tuesday. He said there is no consensus in Washington that conditions are met, adding that the same applies to Seoul’s nuclear submarine ambitions and its U.S. investment pledge. “There is no consensus in Washington, for example, that conditions are ready for wartime OPCON to be transferred,” Yun, who also served as the State Department’s special representative for North Korea policy, said during the second Korea-U.S. Diplomatic Forum, which he joined remotely from the U.S. “Conditions are factors. results.title: Korea employs AI to boost detection, removal of child sexual abuse material
results.content: Korea has adopted an artificial intelligence (AI) system to strengthen detection and removal of online child sexual abuse material, the gender equality and family ministry said Tuesday. The National Center for Digital Sexual Crime Response introduced the AI-powered system in April as Seoul seeks to better counter evolving digital sex crimes in a highly connected country. The center found 96,210 child sexual abuse materials and notified online platforms to remove them between April and September, or about 202.1 cases a day, compared with last year's daily average of 20.8, according to the ministry. The round-the-clock system allows real-time detection of illegal material on online platforms, including social media and random chat apps, reducing the workload on employees at the center who had previously monitored them in person. results.title: Korea Times Translation Awards bring Korean literature closer to world readers
results.content: The Korea Times honored five winning translators during the 57th Modern Korean Literature Translation Awards ceremony held in Seoul Tuesday, celebrating their roles in connecting Korean writers with global readers as artificial intelligence raises new questions about the future of literary translation. Held at the Korea Press Center in Seoul, the ceremony brought together translators, cultural officials and publishing representatives, with speakers emphasizing the human sensitivity needed to carry a work’s emotional depth across languages. The awards are organized by The Korea Times and supported by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and KB Financial Group. The Korea Times President-Publisher Oh Young-jin said the growing international reach of Korean culture coincides with a technological upheaval that demands reflection on what makes literature meaningful. “In this age when ma

results.title: Work on southern section of inter-Korean railway to resume soon: Seoul
results.content: Vice Unification Minister Kim Nam-jung said Tuesday construction will soon resume on the South Korean section of a railway line meant to link the two Koreas. He made the remarks during a seminar in Seoul, as the government seeks to restore the South Korean section of the Gyeongwon Line, which once connected Seoul and North Korea's eastern port city of Wonsan. The last stop now accessible on the southern section is Cheorwon's Baekmagoji in Gangwon Province, and the ministry plans to resume work on the stretch between Baekmagoji and Woljeong-ri Station, the northernmost station on the South Korean side, close to the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) separating the two Koreas. The planned restoration work is aimed at "preparing a path connecting the two Koreas," Kim said at the forum on peace tourism cooperation on the Korean Peninsula. results.title: From Rolex to gold bars, tax-seized luxury goods go up for auction
results.content: Rolex watches, Hermès handbags and gold bars are among 99 lots of luxury goods seized from Korea’s major tax delinquents that will go under the hammer this weekend in a special auction organized by the National Tax Service, Seoul Auction said Tuesday. The sale, scheduled for Saturday, carries combined opening bids of 344.7 million won ($258,000) and will be split between online and in-person bidding, with offerings ranging from fine jewelry and premium whisky to high-end bicycles. Eighteen lots featuring sought-after brands will be available exclusively in person at Seoul Auction’s Gangnam Center. They include a Rolex Day-Date automatic watch with an opening bid of 35 million won and an Hermès Kelly 25 bag with palladium hardware starting at 12 million won. results.title: 'Is Korea desperate enough?'
results.content: The streets of Seoul are already bright with colorful lights and decorations for Christmas. Splashes of red and green and the glitter of small lights create a sense of abundance and festivity. The celebratory ambiance sits uncomfortably, however, here in the capital of one of Asia's export powerhouses. Korea has enjoyed a stellar export rally this year, yet the benefits have yet to materialize as improvements in the cost of living for everyday citizens. A social media post by Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan on Saturday is raising the alarm over the jarring economic landscape. Returning from a three-day trip to China, Kim posted to Facebook: "Are we desperate enough? Are we doing what is required?" results.title: Veteran pianist Paik Kun-woo urges young musicians to seek wider musical world
results.content: Pianist Paik Kun-woo on Tuesday urged young musicians to broaden their musical horizons and find their own artistic paths, ahead of the release of an autobiography marking the 70th anniversary of his career. Paik, one of Korea's most celebrated classical musicians, made his debut performing a piano concerto with a local orchestra in 1956 at age 10. He later trained at New York's Juilliard School and built an international career through performances at prestigious concert halls and collaborations with renowned orchestras and conductors. Reflecting on a career spanning seven decades, Paik is set to publish the autobiography, roughly translated as "Paik Kun-woo: My Story," on Nov. 20. The autobiography traces his childhood, studies in New York, decades spent in Europe and his musical encounters with the works of composers including Beethoven, Chopin and Schumann. results.title: Kolmar Korea's AI lipstick system wins CES beauty tech award
results.content: Kolmar Korea's artificial intelligence (AI)-powered lipstick system, ChromaFlow, won the Best of Innovation award in the beauty technology category for CES 2027, marking the first case of consecutive wins in the category, the company said Tuesday. ChromaFlow also received an Innovation Award in the AI category, while its LumiJet Pro skin care device won another award in that category, bringing Kolmar Korea’s total honors at CES 2027 to three across two products. The company said the recognition follows its award for the Scar Beauty Device, an AI-based wound care and makeup coverage device, at CES 2026. It plans to exhibit both award-winning products at the Venetian Expo in Las Vegas during CES 2027, scheduled for Jan. 6 to 9. results.title: Seoul exhibitions turn discarded materials into design treasures
results.content: Seoul is turning discarded clothing, plastic and industrial waste into functional art and design objects, with two new exhibitions inviting visitors to rethink how everyday products are made, used and thrown away. Organized jointly by the Seoul Metropolitan Government and the Seoul Design Foundation, the dual showcases are hosted on the first floor of the Seoul Upcycling Plaza. Together, they trace the journey of transforming trash into high-value goods while encouraging more environmentally conscious consumer choices. The first exhibition, “Forms of Circularity: Resource Circulation Process,” opened Nov. 2 and runs through April 17, 2027. It highlights innovative recycling systems and commercial products developed by eight participating brands and artists. results.title: Korea repeats principle of non-involvement in Iran war
results.content: Korea's foreign ministry on Tuesday reiterated its principle of "non-involvement" in the war between the United States, Israel and Iran after Tehran called on Seoul to refrain from sending its troops to help reopen the crucial Strait of Hormuz. On Monday, Iran's foreign ministry urged Korea to avoid getting involved in the war, as Seoul plans to expand the operational scope of its anti-piracy Cheonghae unit off the Somali coast to waters closer to the Hormuz strait, a key energy shipping route effectively blocked amid the Iran war. "The (Seoul) government is proceeding with a motion to strengthen the mission of the Cheonghae unit under non-involvement, non-intervention principles for protecting our citizens and economic interests," a ministry official said. results.title: How spicy is too spicy? Korea tests popular instant noodles
results.content: Spicy instant noodles in Korea range from mildly kicky to tear-inducingly hot — and some pack more than a full day’s worth of salt into a single bowl, according to a consumer report released Tuesday by the Korea Consumer Agency. The state-run watchdog conducted a comprehensive safety and quality assessment of 12 top-selling instant noodle products. The test group comprised seven traditional soup-based ramyeon products and five brothless, stir-fried varieties, evaluating them across key metrics including spiciness intensity, nutritional content, safety standards and retail pricing. Laboratory analysis revealed that the concentration of capsaicinoids — the natural chemical compounds in chili peppers responsible for their fiery burn — varied by nearly seven times among the tested brands. results.title: 'Honey trap': Nvidia spy scandal puts Korea on alert
results.content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a Chinese woman accused of spying for Beijing has emerged as a significant national security concern for the United States. According to U.S. intelligence officials, Alice Huang, who worked as a business executive at Singapore-based data center firm Megaspeed in 2023, allegedly collected intelligence and passed it on to China. The scandal erupted amid an intensifying race between the U.S. and China for global leadership in artificial intelligence (AI). The case has served as a wake-up call for South Korea. results.title: Students from 30 countries gather in Seoul to learn Korean language and culture
results.content: Ninety-two students and teachers from 30 countries wrapped up a five-day immersive camp hosted by the Ministry of Education. A group of 92 secondary school students and teachers from 30 countries completed a five-day immersive journey into Korean language and culture, concluding a nationwide youth camp organized by the Ministry of Education. To mark the end of the 2026 International Korean Education Youth Camp, the ministry and the International Korean Education Foundation held a celebratory ceremony Tuesday evening at Sarangjae, a traditional guest house on the National Assembly grounds in Seoul. Running from Friday to Tuesday across Seoul and Incheon, the camp brought together students enrolled in Korean language classes at their home schools. This year’s cohort welcomed its first-ever participant from Mexico, alongside students from Malaysia and Uzbekistan who were recently featured i

results.title: Shinsegae Q3 net income soars 146.4% to $88.5 mil.
results.content: Shinsegae, the operator of Korea's major department store chain, on Tuesday reported its third-quarter net profit of 119 billion won ($88.5 million), a 146.4 percent jump from a year earlier. The retailer said in a regulatory filing that operating profit for the July-September period increased 64.7 percent on-year to 164.3 billion won. Revenue also inched up 1.2 percent to 1.65 trillion won. The earnings exceeded market expectations. The average estimate of net profit by analysts stood at 84.5 billion won, according to a survey by Yonhap Infomax, the financial data firm of Yonhap News Agency.

results.title: 10 winners named at inaugural 2026 Seoul Design Honors awards
results.content: Seoul named 10 individuals and companies as recipients of its inaugural Seoul Design Honors, recognizing projects that have improved public spaces, strengthened the city's identity and made everyday life safer and more accessible for residents. The Seoul Metropolitan Government held the 2026 Seoul Design Honors ceremony Tuesday at City Hall, presenting mayoral commendations to four individuals and six companies selected from 49 nominations. The honors were established to recognize contributions to design development and encourage work that puts people at the center of urban design, drawing inspiration from two Korean cultural achievements: the angbuilgu, an ancient sundial, and "Hunminjeongeum," the original Korean alphabet. results.title: Genesis GV90 sets sights on BMW, Mercedes-Benz in full-size luxury SUV market
results.content: Genesis is stepping up competition in the full-size luxury SUV market with the full-electric GV90, taking aim at German rivals — BMW and Mercedes-Benz — as it seeks to carve out a bigger share of the lucrative high-end segment. The brand unveiled on Tuesday pricing for the GV90, its first full-size flagship SUV, starting at 139.5 million won ($103,000) in Korea. This places the vehicle in a similar price range to the BMW X7 and Mercedes-Benz GLS, positioning Genesis to compete directly for buyers who have traditionally favored German luxury SUVs. The launch represents a significant test for Genesis, which has spent years building its reputation as a premium brand, but has yet to establish the same level of recognition as BMW and Mercedes-Benz in the upper reaches of the luxury market.
